Public Comment: The public is encouraged to address the Planning Commission on any matter listed on the agenda or on any other matter
within its jurisdiction subject to the rules and proceedings described in Section 2.16.060 of the Norwalk Municipal Code. If you wish to address
the Planning Commission, please complete the card that is provided at the rear entrance to Council Chambers and hand the card to the
Secretary. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on items listed on the agenda during discussion of the matter and prior to a
vote. The Planning Commission will hear public comment on matters not listed on the agenda during the Oral Communications period.

Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless certain emergency or
special circumstances exist. The Planning Commission may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a
future Planning Commission meeting.

Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Planning Commission:
   Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
   Comments should be directed to the Planning Commission as a whole and not directed to individual Planning Commission members.

Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City meeting or other services
offered by this City, please contact the Community Development Department, (562) 929-5744. Assisted listening devices are available at this

  NORWALK PLANNING COMMISSION
  NORWALK, CALIFORNIA
  JULY 23, 2025

The meeting was called to order by Chair Lopez at 6:00 p.m., in the Norwalk City Hall,
Council Chambers, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard, Norwalk, California. Present were
Commissioner Barragan, Commissioner Vernola-Salas, Vice Chair Apodaca, and Chair
Lopez. Commissioner Macias was absent. Also present were Alex Hamilton, Interim
Director of Community Development; Nancy Lee, Development Services Manager, Anita
Lakhani, Deputy City Attorney; Kristy Wong, Associate Planner; and Ruth Hoffmann,
Administrative Secretary.

MEETING MINUTES

The Planning Commission approved the minutes of the Special Planning Commission
Meetings of May 14 and June 25, 2025.

PRECISE DEVELOPMENT PLAN (PDP) NO. 2025-01
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST (DAR) NO. 2025-06
DIRECTOR APPROVAL REQUEST (DAR) NO. 2025-07
Scott Wilkeson, McDonald’s USA, LLC (“Applicant”); a request to demolish an existing
2,721 square feet (SF) drive-through restaurant to construct a new 2,123± SF dual order
point drive-through lane restaurant (McDonald’s) improved with an off-street parking lot,
ornamental landscaping, and associated infrastructure on a 0.51-acres lot. The subject
property is generally known as 12959 Rosecrans Avenue, located west of Shoemaker
Avenue and north of Rosecrans Avenue (also known as Assessor’s Parcel Number
(APN) 8046-002-032), in the Restricted Commercial (C-1) zone.
Environmental: Consider and find that the project is exempt from the California
Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15302 (Replacement or
Reconstruction).
The project includes a request for:
PDP 2025-01: To construct a new 2,123± SF dual order point drive-through lane
restaurant (McDonald’s) improved with an off-street parking lot, ornamental
landscaping, and associated infrastructure on a 0.51-acres lot;
DAR 2025-06: To permit the operation of a drive-through establishment; and
DAR 2025-07: To deviate from required landscaping standards.

Chair Lopez opened the public hearing.

Interim Director Hamilton shared that the applicant’s development team is in attendance
tonight along with their technical experts. Further, he stated that he would like to
acknowledge that it has been a pleasure to work with them; and that they have been
incredibly responsive to staff requests.
 Norwalk Planning Commission  Page 2
Minutes of the Special Meeting  July 23, 2025

Staff presented the legal requisites for notice of hearing. Associate Planner Wong
presented a report stating that the proposed request is to demolish the existing 2,721
square foot commercial structure occupied by Kentucky Fried Chicken, and construct a
new 2,123± square foot drive-through restaurant operated by McDonald’s; that the
project will consist of a dual order point drive-through without a dining area; that the site
will be improved with an off-street parking lot, ornamental landscaping, and associated
infrastructure improvements; that a total of eleven (11) off-street parking spaces will be
provided, including one (1) accessible parking space and four (4) future EV capable
spaces; that short-term bicycle parking spaces are also provided; that the double drive-
through lane will accommodate a total of ten (10) queuing spaces from the pickup
window; that the site can be accessed by two driveways, the primary one along
Rosecrans Avenue and a secondary access along Shoemaker Avenue.

Continuing with her presentation, Ms. Wong shared that the proposed restaurant is
providing an “On the Go” concept with only a drive-through with two order points and
delivery and mobile service pickup windows for pedestrians; that no walk-up ordering is
allowed, and no dining area is offered; that it is going to be a 24-hour operation, open
daily; that the conditions of approval include a condition that traffic from the drive-
through not back up onto public streets, and that the menu board have noise reduction
technology; that a deviation of approximately 192 square feet, or 3.4 percent, of required
landscaping is requested to accommodate internal traffic circulation; that in
consideration of this deviation request, the project complies with all other development
standards; that it will enhance the surrounding area by revitalizing a site, incorporating
quality architecture and promoting economic activity; that the project also complies with
applicable city codes and, with the recommended conditions of approval, provides
adequate parking, vehicular circulation, and pedestrian access.

Ms. Wong stated that it is staff’s recommendation that the Planning Commission adopt
Resolution Nos. 25-08, 25-09 and 25-10 to approve the applicant’s request subject to
the conditions of approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and consider and find that the project
is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section
15302 (Replacement or Reconstruction).

The applicant’s representative, Robert Preece, Design UA, Inc. stated that, first he
would like to thank staff for their efforts in bringing this project before the Commission.
Further, he added that, as stated, this is a drive-through only restaurant with walk-up
windows for mobile orders or delivery service providers; that no walk-up ordering is
allowed; that the site will be fully developed to include new landscaping, paving, and
parking.

Since there were no other persons wishing to present testimony, Chair Lopez closed
the public hearing.

Commissioner Barragan stated that she likes the building design and lighting.

Commissioner Vernola-Salas indicated that this new concept is a good idea, that it’s
simple, and generates less traffic for the neighborhood.

In response to Vice Chair Apodaca’s question what happens when a person walks up
and tries to order as they are not aware of this new concept, Mr. Preece indicated that,
typically, staff will walk out and guide them on the process. Vice Chair Apodaca stated
that the development will improve that corner, and that it is a great location.

Chair Lopez stated that she agrees that it is a great concept, and she asked if there are
similar McDonald’s in Los Angeles County or throughout the nation, Mr. Preece replied
that more “On the Go” concept McDonald’s are coming to Los Angeles County to fill the
gap; that the Norwalk project is the second one in the State of California, and that the
first one was opened in Bellflower.

It was moved by Vice Chair Apodaca and seconded by Commissioner Vernola-Salas
to: (a) Adopt Resolution No. 25-08 to approve Precise Development Plan (PDP) No.
2025-01 subject to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; (b) Adopt
Resolution No. 25-09 to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2025-06 subject
to the Conditions of Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; (c) Adopt Resolution No. 25-10
to approve Director Approval Request (DAR) No. 2025-07 subject to the Conditions of
Approval contained in Exhibit “A”; and (d) Consider and find that the project is exempt
from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines pursuant to Section
15302 (Replacement or Reconstruction).

Commission and City Council for their support.

Authority:
Section 17.02.210 (“Conditional Use Permits”) of the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”)
authorizes the Planning Commission of the City of Norwalk (“Planning Commission”) to
grant a conditional use permit for those uses which are allowed and in granting a
conditional use permit, may impose such conditions as it determines necessary and
reasonable to protect the best interests of the surrounding property or neighborhood and
ensure the degree of compatibility required is maintained with respect to the particular
use on the particular site, giving consideration to other existing and potential uses within
the general area.

Section 17.02.203 (“Director Approval Request”) of the NMC requires the filing of a
Director Approval Request (DAR) to approve minor developments, including façade
improvements on properties zoned for nonresidential uses and sets forth the findings that
the Director of Community Development (“Director”) shall make prior to the approval of a
DAR.

Section 17.02.203.B of the NMC authorizes the Director at his or her discretion to refer
any DAR request to the Planning Commission for review. Specifically, since the CUP
requires Planning Commission review, the DAR was referred to the Planning Commission
to be reviewed concurrently with the CUP.
Introduction/background:

The subject site is located at 11642 Firestone Boulevard (APN: 8048-007-002). The
subject site is approximately 43,000± square feet in size and has a General Plan land use
designation of General Commercial and zoning classification of C-3 (General
Commercial). The subject site is situated on the southside of Firestone Boulevard, west
of Pioneer Boulevard and east of Orr and Day Road.

Per the Los Angeles County Assessor’s records, the subject site is currently developed
with a 9,765 square foot office building constructed in 1955. City records reflect that the
building was previously occupied by a real estate company.

The subject property is located on a major thoroughfare within a developed area. The
property is surrounded by Specific Plan Area (SPA) No. 14 zone to the north and C-3
(General Commercial) to the east, south, and west.
Project Description:

Juliette Fralick (“Applicant”), on behalf of David’s Place, LLC., is requesting approval of
 CUP No. 2025-01 to establish and operate a social services use for developmentally
 disabled clients on the subject site within an existing 9,765 square foot office building on
 a 43,000+ square foot site. The existing building will be renovated with associated site

improvements.
The applicant is also requesting approval of DAR No. 2025-12 to allow for a façade
improvement consisting of a new entryway along the front elevation of the building along
with off-site improvements, including parking lot paving and enhanced landscaping in the
C-3 zone.

Site Development
The applicant proposes to rehabilitate an existing 9,765 square foot office building for a
social service use for developmentally disabled clients with associated site
improvements. The Project also includes a modification to the façade for a new entry
along Firestone Boulevard. The site will include the installation of approximately 2,170 SF
in landscaping improvements, improvements in the parking lot and pavement, and the
improvement of an existing trash enclosure located at the southwest area of the site.

Site Circulation & Off-Street Parking
The subject site currently has two primary vehicle ingress and egress access points
located along Firestone Boulevard. One driveway is located in the western most area of
the site is approximately 39 feet in width. The other driveway is located along the eastern
frontage and is approximately 37 feet in width.
Based on the proposed use, 44 off-street parking spaces are required per NMC Section
17.03.040. A total of 46 parking spaces are provided including two (2) ADA accessible
parking spaces. Vehicles entering through the western entrance will be able to access
the parking area on the west of the site, the north side, and eastern parking areas. The
eastern most entrance will allow vehicles to access the parking areas to the east of the
site and those situated on the north side of the site.
Clients will either be picked-up or dropped off by family, utilize public transportation or be
transported via a service van operated by David’s Place. There will be a maximum of
three transportation vans. For the pick-ups and drop-offs, a parking stall will be
designated for such. A staff person will also assist to ensure both are conducted in a safe
manner. For clients taking the bus, there are multiple bus stops near the intersection of
Firestone Boulevard and Pioneer Boulevard.

Floor Plan
The floor plan consists of multiple offices, kitchen area, laundry, fitness room, creative
activities room, conference room, and common space designed to be functional and
suitable for the proposed use. The layout is constructed in a way conducive to the
proposed use, equally considerate of the clients, staff and management. The proposed
use and the rehabilitation of the existing building will allow for the provision of services
and foster the success of clients.

Architectural Design
The proposed use will occupy an existing office, commercial building that is a Spanish
colonial influenced with a stucco exterior, brick veneer, with semi-circle porch ways with
eight columns. The proposed project will involve a minor modification by creating a new
entryway consistent with the other existing entrance with a gable roof, similar roof and
pitch. The improvements will also involve an upgrade to building exterior, including the
repairing and replacement of the existing siding, fascia, brick veneer and involve
repainting as well. The minor façade improvement will ensure consistency with the overall
building and a uniform architectural style.

Landscaping
The subject site will consist of improvements to an existing landscaped area of 2,170
square feet in size. In addition, 864 square feet of public right-of-way landscaping
improvements are proposed. Per the NMC, landscaping is required in the setback areas
and 25 square feet of landscaping for each parking space provided which would total
1,150 square feet for 46 parking spaces. Additionally, due to the project involving an
existing building there are no new additional landscaping requirements. The project would
also be subject to the Model Water Efficient Landscape Ordinance (MWELO) and the
City’s landscape requirements.

Business Operations
The proposed use will serve developmentally disabled adults with co-occurring
development disabilities. A structured and supportive environment will facilitate the
assistance and support of social development, vocational training, independent living
skills, and employment readiness to participants. The program will have two sessions
daily Monday through Friday with the first from 8:30 am to 12:30 p.m. and the second
session from 1:30 p.m. to 5:30 p.m. A full program will serve up to 30 participants at any
given time with 10 support staff (2:1 ratio) that will include counseling services, direct
support personnel and administrative support. These services are designed to be
inclusive, support the independence, and personal growth of individuals. This location will
operate under the Non-medical Adult-day program which is licensed by the California
Department of Social Services, through its community care licensing division. This is the
third location for David’s Place as the other two facilities are located in Long Beach
(Attachment F, Operations Narrative).

The subject property has a General Plan land use designation of General Commercial,
which is intended to provide for the wide range of commercial goods and services. The
proposed social service facility is consistent with the General Plan’s goals and policies of
the land use element.

Entitlements:

Conditional Use Permit
In the C-3 (General Commercial) Zone, social service uses are permitted with a
Conditional Use Permit. The purpose of requiring a conditional use permit is to ensure that
the degree of compatibility required is maintained and respected with a particular use on
the particular site, providing consideration to other existing and potential uses within the
general area in which the use is located or proposed. Additionally, the proposed project
shall comply with all applicable C-3 development standards and ensure compliance and
consistency with the general plan while ensuring the best interests of the surrounding
neighborhood or neighborhood are maintained and where any conditions may be imposed
by the Planning Commission.
The proposed project and use of a social services facility will benefit the community,
rehabilitate a vacant building, occupy an underutilized parcel and provide much needed
services to developmentally disabled adults and their families and ensure compatibility
with the neighborhood.

Director Approval Request
The purpose of the Director Approval Request to provide a streamlined process for
administrative approval of certain requests to encourage existing property and business
owners to invest and make improvements to their buildings, properties and facilitate their
success, while ensuring that they meet the intent of the General Plan and the NMC. The
proposed use is consistent with the General Plan as it provides the essential daily needs
of the surrounding residential area.

Minor developments – Façade improvements on properties zoned for nonresidential uses.
The applicant proposes to make a minor façade modification at the front (north) elevation
facing Firestone Boulevard for a new additional front entry. The proposal will enhance the
curb appeal and include a new entry that is functional and beneficial for participants. The
façade improvement and the project complies with all other development standards,
improves an existing commercial site and enhances the commercial corridor along
Firestone Boulevard by stimulating business activity and occupying an underutilized and
vacant site.

Public Notification:
Notice of this public hearing was published in The Norwalk Patriot and posted at the City’s
three designated posting sites and the City website on September 11, 2025, as well as
mailed to 47 property owners and interested parties within 500 feet of the property on
Thursday, September 11, 2025.
Environmental Assessment:

Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines Section 15301,
the proposed façade improvements and establishment and operation of a Social Service
use will not have a significant effect on the environment per Sections 15301 (Existing
Facilities). The Class 1 Categorical Exemption consists of the operation and minor
alteration of existing private structures involving negligible or no expansion of existing or
former use.

The proposed project involves the rehabilitation and reuse of an existing 9,765 square foot
office building and associated site improvements (including but not limited to façade
improvements, off-street parking lot and enhanced landscaping) to establish and operate
a social services use within an existing building for developmentally disabled clients on a
43,000+ square foot site. The building will undergo a tenant improvement, façade
modification and parking lot improvements. The proposed project would not intensify land
use or increase service capacity beyond what exists on-site, and the reuse of the building
with no square footage being added does not require additional compliance with building
codes, etc. The project would remain consistent with the City’s General Plan and zoning
designations, and it would continue an existing land use within a fully developed, urbanized
area.

Accordingly, the proposed project satisfies the criteria for a Class 1 Categorical Exemption
under CEQA Guidelines Section 15301 Existing Facilities as it involves operation and the
minor alteration of existing private structures involving negligible or no expansion of
existing or a former use.
Recommendation:

The Proposed Use is anticipated to have a positive impact to the surrounding
neighborhood and the city of Norwalk as the proposed use of a social services facility will
benefit the community, rehabilitate a vacant building, occupy an underutilized parcel and
provide much needed services to developmentally disabled adults and their families and
ensure compatibility with the neighborhood. The project complies with applicable City
codes and based on submitted reports and recommended conditions of approval, the use
is permitted conditionally, proposes adequate parking, vehicular circulation, and
pedestrian access. Additionally, the project is consistent with the General Plan objectives
and policies of adequate office space in providing a wide range of goods and services.

  WHEREAS, Conditional Use Permit (CUP) No. 2025-01 was submitted by Juliette

approximately 43,000 square feet in size; and

this request for minor façade improvements; and

  WHEREAS, the Subject Site is designated as General Commercial by the City’s

  WHEREAS, the Subject Site is currently located within the zoning classification of
General Commercial (C-3); and

  WHEREAS, the approval of a CUP is required for the proposed use in the C-3 zone;
and

  WHEREAS, the purpose and intent of requiring a CUP is to ensure that the degree
of compatibility required is maintained and respected with a particular use on the particular
site, providing consideration to other existing and potential uses within the general area in
which it is located or proposed; and

  WHEREAS, Section 17.02.210 (Conditional Use Permits) authorizes the Planning
Commission of the City of Norwalk to grant a conditional use permit for those uses which
are allowed and in granting a CUP, may impose such conditions as determined necessary
per the Norwalk Municipal Code (“NMC”) to the Planning Commission for review; and

  WHEREAS, CUP No. 2025-01 has been reviewed by the Planning Commission on

  NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS:
   Section 1. Environmental. That in accordance with the criteria and authority
contained in the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) of 1970 and the CEQA
Guidelines as amended, staff has conducted the appropriate environmental analysis and
based on that assessment, the City has determined that the Proposed Use qualifies for an
Notice of Exemption under Article 19 Categorical Exemptions, Section 15301 (Class 1 –
Existing Facilities) in that the action involves the rehabilitation and reuse of an existing
building.

  Section 2. General Plan. The Proposed Project is consistent with the goals and
objectives of the Norwalk General Plan as the Proposed Project is consistent with General
Commercial land use designation which indicates that this site and this zone is conducive
to a wide range of business establishments. The project will also have a positive impact to
the surrounding neighborhood and benefit the community of Norwalk.

Re: David’s Place CUP Application – Operations Statement

To: Alex Hamilton

Our program in Norwalk will operate as a licensed adult day program serving adults with co-
occurring developmental disabilities. We provide a structured and supportive environment that
emphasizes social development, vocational training, independent living skills, and employment
readiness. The program will operate Monday through Friday with two sessions, the first from
8:30 AM to 12:30 PM and the second from 1:30 PM to 5:30 PM, with administrative staff
occasionally present before or after regular hours for preparation and closing procedures. At full
capacity, the program will serve up to 30 participants per day, supported by 10 on-site staff (2:1
ratio), including counselors, direct support personnel, and administrative team members.
Because not all participants attend five days a week, daily attendance may vary. In addition,
participants regularly engage in community-based activities to build real-life skills, which may
also impact their on-site presence throughout the week.

Program services will include life skills instruction, employment preparation, recreational and
art-based activities, supervised community outings, and volunteer opportunities in the local
community. The program will also incorporate positive behavioral supports into the daily
structure to help participants develop coping strategies and manage challenges in a respectful,
non-clinical setting. These services are designed to promote inclusion, independence, and
personal growth while meeting the unique needs of each individual. Participants will be dropped
off and picked up by family members, ride-share services, or agency-operated vans. Staff will
utilize designated parking located on-site.

The program will be located at 11642 Firestone Blvd, Norwalk 90652, in a single-story
commercial unit that includes designated areas for group activities, vocational training, a staff
break room, administrative offices, and accessible restrooms. Most activities are conducted
indoors, and noise levels remain low to moderate. The facility will be secured with a controlled
access system. All visitors will be required to sign in, and participants will be supervised at all
times. Staff will be trained in emergency protocols, and fire drills and safety trainings will be
conducted regularly. The facility will be cleaned daily, with waste disposal handled in
accordance with city guidelines. Cleaning supplies are securely stored in locked cabinets.

  1870 ATLANTIC AVENUE, LONG BEACH, CA 90806
 The Norwalk location will operate under a Non-Medical Adult Day Program (ADP) license issued
by the California Department of Social Services (CDSS) through its Community Care Licensing
Division. This license covers the provision of supervision, personal care, meals, and structured
activities for adults age 18 and older, including individuals with developmental disabilities. In
addition to licensing, the program will complete the required vendorization process with the
Regional Center in order to serve individuals receiving services through California’s
developmental services system. This vendorization process is coordinated through the
California Department of Developmental Services in partnership with the appropriate Regional
Center. The program will comply with all applicable staff training and certification requirements,
including certification for the program administrator, the hiring of qualified direct care staff,
criminal background clearances,, and adherence to staff-to-client ratios and safety protocols.

We currently operate two adult day program locations in Long Beach. David’s Place 1, at 1870
Atlantic Avenue, Long Beach, Ca 90806, operates from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and serves
approximately 60 participants daily. This program focuses on supporting individuals in social
development, health and wellness, and independent living skills. David’s Place 2, at 4800 E. Los
Coyotes Diagonal, Ste 102, Long Beach, Ca 90815, operates from 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM and
serves approximately 30 participants per day. This site emphasizes the development of soft
skills for employment and provides hands-on experience through active community volunteering
opportunities. Both locations maintain full compliance with Regional Center requirements.

We are committed to operating a high-quality, compliant program that meets the needs of our
participants and aligns with the city’s standards. We appreciate your consideration and look
forward to moving ahead with this project.
